newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Ford Australia to review investment if tariffs cut.
newsitem.headline: Ford Australia to review investment if tariffs cut.

text.p: Ford Australia said on Tuesday it would review its investment plans in Australia if a government industry review recommended that tariffs for the industry were cut below their current 15 percent level.
"All we have said so far is we would have to look at our investment plans if the tariff goes below 15 percent," said Ford Australia managing director David Morgan.

Morgan told a business luncheon that the industry needed to achieve a pause in the process of reducing tariffs and needed the continuation of the export facilitation scheme to provide the critical mass the industry required to survive.

The car industry is lobbying against a proposal by the Productivity Commission to lower tariffs to five percent by 2004. Tariffs are scheduled already to fall from the current 22.5 percent to 15 percent by 2000.
Japanese car makers Mitsubishi Motors Australia Ltd and Toyota Motor Corp Australia both recently reported losses for their Australian operations.
